analysis:
Examined all six batch analyses and independently checked the replayed patches. No concrete security regression is supported by the available evidence. In provider-ci-build/action.yml HEAD 64–181 and provider-release-build/action.yml HEAD 120–392, CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off gates the changed cache restores/saves, not the surrounding build, test or validation steps. ci-master.yml HEAD 77–143 and 227–290 sets that flag before caching and screens restored .git metadata before Git validation/checkout. This resolves the earlier local question about cache-selection ordering in those jobs. The screening adds protections; it does not prove arbitrary Git configuration is inert, but incomplete hardening of the pre-existing cache path is not itself a new vulnerability.
Across the batches, reported changes concern CI caching, runner routing, test sizing and unsigned desktop packaging. No supplied runtime change establishes weakened serving authorization, attestation, hop encryption, prompt isolation, billing or privileged-helper controls. Actions caches and documented test buffer limits are distinct from T-041's production encrypted prefix cache. Build provenance remains relevant to A-011/A-017 and T-013/T-054; runner/test availability is relevant to A-018.
Material integration uncertainty remains: the replay omits 51 of 54 source units, so assertions about provider-plan.yml HEAD 174–185, desktop.yml HEAD 61–95 and provider-tests.yml routing/cache consumers cannot all be independently verified here. Review the new routing/cache contract for approved runner identity and isolation, cache endpoint authentication and trusted-versus-PR writer separation, and any path from routed build outputs into qualified releases. Confirm logged DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL values contain no credentials. The supplied evidence establishes neither attacker control of these services nor unsafe artifact promotion; these are unresolved contracts, not findings. Reduced lane sizes alone do not establish a security-relevant failure.
